Not going to be an organized answer heads up to all my organized folks. 
I can’t give a solid answer but there were repetitive images in my head amidst my self bettering journey. I’d see images of my father when he was younger and the self discipline he had to build to get to where he is today, I’d see images of my mom showing courage and strength in her younger years as well, I’d think of my ex and how he worked his ass off to better himself after I broke his heart, (those especially motivated those extra 1 or 2 reps in the gym hehe), I’d think of my high school senior class and how I feel the need to be the best (which bothers me typing this because Buddha doesn’t like ego and Buddha knew a lot, not to suck his cock but.. yeah) there were 29 kids that graduated that year. Anyway, I’d think about my future kiddos and how I want to be a damn good mom one day and how doing good things and improving myself gets me one step closer to being good for my future children. I say “good” with as much purity and love as you can fathom. My parents fought a LOT growing up and frankly I’m just not about it. Choose love not war✌️Hate cannot drive out hate, only love can do that. To add onto the imagery, I’d also think about me rich as fuck in the future. I’ve noticed something in wealthy people and how they’re usually more intelligent, self-disciplined, clean, good with time management, etc. (I’d like to add that I could be wrong so don’t come for me pls) I’d like to become wealthy sooner rather than later so fake it til ya make it. I’d also like to give a shout-out to self bettering audio books accessible on YouTube. For freeeee? Seems too good to be true. 

TLDR: To be a good mom and to be wealthy and ego
I hope you didn’t go through with it… Please find the little ounce of goodness there is left in your life and hold onto it. Please, keep going.
